svg.title: danielgarcia.it: from the career YAML files to the HTML pages
svg.text: Career data: from data/career/*.yml to the HTML pages
How Maven, Quarkus and Roq turn the YAML files into Java records, then into a CDI bean that the Qute templates read.
typed in the VS Code terminal
no questions, no colours or progress
bars, as on the CI server.
run every phase up to package.
the phases run by package, in this order
javac turns the .java records into .class files
runs SiteTest, which starts the application: Quarkus runs its build, including Roq
builds the final application; only reached if every test passes
in the test phase when SiteTest starts the application, then in the package phase · Roq data extension: RoqDataReaderProcessor, RoqDataConverterProcessor
file name without extension = language code
Top-level keys: profile, experience, education, certifications,
a record is an immutable data class
One component per YAML key, same name: experience holds Experience records,
skillGroups holds SkillGroup records… Compact constructors check the dates.
Jandex index of the compiled classes
required: fails if it is empty.
Stops the build if a key has no
component or a date is wrong:
Roq puts the records in a map
writes it as JSON, then reads it
Jackson also writes get…() and is…()
CDI bean, created at build time
so the map goes into byLanguage.
when Roq generates the HTML pages
the List<Experience> of fr.yml, used in {#for} loops
Same template for both languages: only lang in the front matter of the page changes.
At step 3, Jackson treats a method named
as a property and writes "current" in the JSON.
On reading, "current" is not a component
of Experience, and failOnUnknownProperties rejects it.
Without the is/get prefix, the method stays
out of the JSON: current(), hasReference().
